title: Compact representation of strongly correlated Green's functions: the MOR+EC way to explore phase space
authors: Norman Hogan, A. F. Kemper, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera
abstract: Repeated evaluation of the single-particle Green's function (GF) across parameter space is a recurring bottleneck in many-body methods, limiting the resolution at which phase boundaries may be probed and the frequency resolution of computed spectra. We introduce MOR+EC, a framework that constructs reusable reduced-order models for computing single-particle Green's functions by combining eigenvector continuation (EC) for parameter space exploration and model order reduction (MOR) for extrapolation in frequency space. Contrary to conventional parameterized MOR, we construct these reduced-order models with a parameter-independent resolvent, further reducing the number of required full-space evaluations. Benchmarking against exact diagonalization as the impurity solver for our example case of DMFT calculations for single- and two-band models, MOR+EC reproduces the DMFT-converged impurity GF to an average relative error of $\sim10^{-4}$, with a median wall-time speedup of $16-91\times$. This accuracy and efficiency together resolve a fine-grained scan of the impurity occupation as doping is tuned and produce a high-resolution phase diagram of an orbital-selective Mott transition. The reduced-order model also reproduces real- and imaginary-frequency spectra at no additional cost in full-space evaluations. This framework applies broadly to GF-based methods requiring repeated parametric evaluation and high resolution of the frequency axis.
summary: This paper introduces MOR+EC, a novel framework that combines Model Order Reduction and Eigenvector Continuation to create compact, reusable models for calculating Green's functions. By drastically reducing the computational cost of repeated evaluations, the method allows for high-resolution mapping of complex phase diagrams in strongly correlated electron systems studied via DMFT. This represents a significant computational advance for theoretical condensed matter physics.
main_problem: Repeated evaluation of the single-particle Green's function across parameter space is a major computational bottleneck in many-body methods.
main_result: The MOR+EC framework achieves high accuracy (relative error $\sim 10^{-4}$) with massive speedups ($16-91	imes$), enabling fine-grained phase diagram mapping.
method: The authors combine Model Order Reduction (MOR) for frequency extrapolation and Eigenvector Continuation (EC) for parameter space exploration to build a compact, reusable reduced-order model.
model_or_system: The framework is applied to strongly correlated materials studied via Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) using single- and two-band impurity models.
key_observables: Single-particle Green's function (GF), impurity self-energy ($\Sigma_{	ext{imp}}$), and real/imaginary-frequency spectra.
important_parameters: Doping, temperature, and the frequency axis ($z$ or $i\omega_n$).
main_assumptions: The reduced-order model construction relies on the assumption that the system's physics can be accurately captured by a low-dimensional subspace spanned by sampled snapshots.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the combination of EC (for ground state basis B) and MOR (for GF representation) to build ROMs for dense phase space exploration, applied to DMFT.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the computational bottleneck, introducing the MOR+EC combination, detailing the adaptive basis construction (global/local enrichment), and finally demonstrating its successful application to the DMFT self-consistency loop.
why_interesting: The efficiency gains achieved by reducing the dimensionality of the parameter and frequency space are highly relevant for any simulation involving repeated calculations of spectral functions or response properties in open quantum systems.
